title: Niryasa 7. The Resolution of the Doubt concerning the Passing of Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami
html:
The author asks Hemalata: the Prema-vilasa says that the Kaviraja died of grief at the news of the theft of the books, and Raghunatha Dasa even earlier, whereas the Kaviraja himself writes that Raghunatha is alive; Hemalata relates Srinivasa's answer to Ramachandra: Raghunatha, bound by his vow, could not depart before his time, while the Kaviraja, hearing the command of Rupa and Sanatana, returned to his body

1Glory, glory to Mahaprabhu, the deliverance of the fallen!
Glory, glory to Nityananda, the treasury of compassion!

2Glory, glory to the Lord of Sita, Ishvara Advaita!
Glory, glory to Prabhu's associates headed by Srivasa!

3Glory, glory to Sri Svarupa Gosani Damodara!
Glory, glory to Sri Ramananda, the mine of rasa!

4Glory to Rupa and Sanatana, purifiers of the fallen!
Glory, glory to the feet of Sri Gopala Bhatta!

5Glory to Raghunatha Bhatta and Sri Dasa Gosani!
Glory, glory for ever to Sri Jiva Gosani!

6Glory to Sri Acharya Prabhu, the ocean of mercy!
Glory, glory to Ramachandra together with his brother!

7Glory to the Vaishnava Gosanis, purifiers of the fallen!
With a straw between my teeth I beg: give me this wealth —

8with longing to attain the feet of Sri Acharya Prabhu;
out of mercy fulfil this desire of mine.

9Listen, listen, devotees, to my request,
hear a most holy account.

10Having heard the book, Prabhu1 was pleased
and, with a softened heart, showed much mercy:

11"Listen, listen, son, I tell you:
in your heart is the shining of my Prabhu's feet."

12Then I, clasping Srimati's two feet,
bowed many times, rolling on the ground:

13"Listen, listen, Prabhu, be merciful to me:
there is a great doubt in my heart.

14If out of mercy you dispel the doubt…"
The words of her holy lips soothe the ears.

15Prabhu says: "Tell me what doubt — I shall listen."
Then I spoke these words to Prabhu's feet:

16"At Jahnava's command Nityananda Dasa
composed the Prema-vilasa on Prabhu's life.2

17When Prabhu came to Gauda with the books,
there he wrote these words in particular:

18that the Kaviraja, hearing the news of the theft of the books,
leapt up, went and fell into the Kunda;3

19most detached at heart, he could not contain himself:
'Alas, alas, such grief cannot be borne!'

20And Sri Dasa Gosvami had left his body even earlier.
Hearing this, doubt arose in my heart.

21Srila Kaviraja Gosani in his own book
wrote in the summaries — I have copied them one by one:

22'May Sri Raghunatha Dasa abide' — so he wrote.4
With great doubt I submitted to your feet:

23Raghunatha disappeared before the Kaviraja —
yet in the summary the great one wrote this word;

24did the Kaviraja depart before Raghunatha?
'When will the Gosani come before my eyes?' —

25such words the Gosani wrote more than once.
The doubt in my heart grew beyond measure;

26with great doubt I submitted to your feet:
out of mercy, Prabhu, dispel the doubt."

27Hearing this, the Thakurani rejoiced greatly at heart
and began to speak sweetly:

28"Listen, son: I heard earlier from Prabhu's5 lips —
Ramachandra asked Prabhu about this very thing,

29and the answer Prabhu gave him
made Ramachandra very happy.

30Being nearby, I heard those words;
all those words I shall tell you in full.

31Prabhu says: 'Ramachandra, hear the word:
I shall tell you something wondrous — listen.

32Who could write down the endless virtues of Raghunatha?
Raghunatha's rules are like a line on stone.

33The Gosvami's vow is most firm and certain:
whatever vow he made cannot be broken.

34In separation from Sri Rupa the Gosani was afflicted at heart;
almost blind, he stayed on the bank of Radha-kunda.

35In great separation the Gosani was afflicted at heart,
thinking unceasingly how to leave his body.

36At that time the news of the theft of the books arrived:
in great grief (the Kaviraja) rose, weeping:6

37"Alas, alas, what has happened — what a great calamity!" —
so he repeated in grief again and again.

38Then that Gosvami could not hold himself;
holding in his heart the lotus feet of Raghunatha,

39he was as if attaining his siddha-deha7 —
and the grief in Dasa Gosvami's heart knew no bounds.

40Thus among all the residents of Radha-kunda
the grief in their hearts greatly increased.

41Then the two brothers, Rupa and Sanatana,
were greatly troubled at heart.

42Knowing the firmness of Raghunatha's vow,
the two Gosvamis speak, calling the Kaviraja:

43"For this purpose is the writing of Prabhu, the Jagad-guru:8
to entrust to Srinivasa the great treasure of the books.

44For this purpose Chaitanya Gosani revealed the books,
infusing shakti into me;

45to distribute them in Gauda — shakti in Srinivasa:
this is the reason, this is Mahaprabhu's command.

46The command of Prabhu, the crown of the all-knowing, is stronger:
who has the power to act otherwise?

47Why do you leave your body in vain from grief?
The books will be found — this I tell you.

48Serve Raghunatha for some days more;
afterwards you will come again into my group."

49Drinking the nectar of the two brothers' command,
the Kaviraja again regained consciousness in his body.

50All the gods in the sky gave their command (by a heavenly voice);
seeing the Kaviraja's return (to life), all are deep in thought:

51"How could Raghunatha's vow be broken?" —
all together pondered this unceasingly.

52The Gosvami's writing is like a line on stone:
who has the power to refute it?

53Of this in the Stavavali, in the Sva-niyama-dashaka, verse 9: "Sustaining my life without pride, by rule, with things born in Vraja — milk for food, clothing, vessels and the rest — I live at the kunda of the Mistress and by the best of hills; and in due time I shall die by the dear lake, before Jiva and the others" etc.9

54"Milk born in Vraja is my food, the leaves of Vraja's trees my clothing;
by these I shall live, giving up pride.

55At Sri Kunda or at Mount Govardhana —
I shall surely die on the bank of Radha-kunda.

56This is a most firm rule, most difficult:
Sri Jiva will be before me,

57and Sri Krishnadasa and Gosani Lokanatha."
Knowing this, suddenly a heavenly voice resounded;

58all heard it with their own ears:
"Listen, listen, Kaviraja, I tell you:
soon you will receive the news that the books have been found."

59The two brothers and the words of the gods
the Kaviraja heard with his own ears.

60The siddha-deha and the body of a practitioner — he had both at once:
the great one regained the body of a practitioner.

61There is evidence of this, hear with one mind:
it is clearly written in the Chaitanya-charitamrita:10

62'In the state of inner consciousness Mahaprabhu
saw the water-pastimes and was absorbed in that bhava:

63in the Yamuna — water-pastimes with the gopis,
Prabhu watches from the bank with the sakhis.

64Meanwhile Svarupa and the others go about searching;
hearing from the lips of a fisherman, they came

65and, seeing Prabhu almost lifeless, were grieved;
Svarupa and the others, anxious,

66loudly chanted the name of Hari into Prabhu's ears —
hearing it, Mahaprabhu regained consciousness.'

67Inner consciousness and outer — this is the evidence:
know in this way what happened with the Kaviraja.

68If one who is perfected (lives) as a practitioner — what is surprising in that?
In the mundane (world) such things never happen;

69therefore all this is very hard to fathom.
Truly firm was this rule of Raghunatha.

70In the Prema-vilasa this was not made clear:
at first something was written, but the end was not written.'

71Hearing this, Ramachandra, with joy in his heart,
fell to the ground like a rod.

72Prabhu placed his own foot on his head
and, rejoicing, raised him and embraced him tightly.

73Prabhu says: 'Listen, Ramachandra Kaviraja:
keep all this deep in your heart.'

74Then Prabhu, taking Sri Ramachandra by the hand,
began to speak sweet words to him:

75'You are like me, possessor of all virtues;
you know my mind — what more can I say?

76No one but you ever knows this;
you are my life — this I have said for certain.

77Whoever accepts my community as you do
will become a vessel of my mercy.

78Whoever hears this account with faith,
that fortunate one obtains the great treasure of prema.

79Raghunatha is the non-different body of Sri Rupa.'
Hearing this, Ramachandra considered himself to have attained his goal.

80All this account that I heard
I have told you in a few syllables.

81What is surprising in what concerns the eternally perfect?
This is a most holy nectar for the ears."

82Hearing so many words from Srimati's lips,
I soothed my soul, filling my ears with them.

83Listen, listen, devotees — this is my request:
the doubt is dispelled, I have relished this.

84Receiving the nectar of command from my mistress's moon-like lips,
I have kept my life, with a contented heart.

85Thus I have told of the resolution of my doubt;
giving up idle argument, always relish this.

86To the company of Sri Acharya Prabhu — millions of obeisances:
out of mercy fulfil the desire of my heart.

87By the mercy of you all every perfection is attained,
prema-bhakti is easily given.

88With the desire to attain the associates of Sri Rupa
let him hear this who has supreme longing.

89Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu with His own associates,
fulfil my desire, all of you, with gracious hearts!

90With the desire to attain the feet of Sri Acharya Prabhu —
out of mercy fulfil this desire.

91The daughter of Sri Acharya Prabhu is Srila Hemalata:
has not the Creator fashioned a wish-fulfilling creeper of prema?

92Her two lotus feet sport in my heart;
Yadunandana Dasa tells the account of the Karnananda.

Thus ends the seventh niryasa of the Sri Karnananda, composed by Sri Yadunandana Dasa Thakura, a Vaidya, resident of the village of Malihati, called "The Resolution, by Srimati Hemalata Thakurani, of the Author's Doubt concerning the Passing of Sri Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami". Thus ends the book Sri Karnananda. May it be auspicious!

May the account of the Karnananda, ever delighting the ears with its sound — (the account of) Sri Srinivasa Prabhu — be heard and heard again with joy!11

Notes

  1. Hemalata.
  2. That is, Srinivasa's life; cf. 6.120–121.
  3. Prema-vilasa 13: Krishnadasa Kaviraja, hearing of the theft of the books, died of grief at Radha-kunda (cf. ev-krishnadasa-kaviraja-departure).
  4. The opening blessing in the CC (the summaries, suchakas, of the chapters, e.g. Antya 1) — bhūyāt śrī-raghunātha-dāsaḥ ("may Raghunatha Dasa abide"): so when the Kaviraja was completing the CC, Raghunatha was alive. The author's doubt is a real contradiction between the Prema-vilasa and the CC.
  5. Srinivasa.
  6. The subject is not named; from the sense of what follows (38–49), it is Krishnadasa Kaviraja.
  7. That is, left his body. This account is an attempt to reconcile the Prema-vilasa with the CC: the Kaviraja supposedly died of grief, but at the command of Rupa and Sanatana returned to his body in order to serve Raghunatha. This reconciliation is found only in the Karnananda.
  8. That is, Mahaprabhu. Rupa and Sanatana speak here from the eternal abode, appearing to the Kaviraja.
  9. Raghunatha Dasa's Sva-niyama-dashaka, v. 9 (cf. 4.446). Raghunatha's vow was to die before the eyes of Jiva, Krishnadasa and Lokanatha; therefore Krishnadasa could not depart before him.
  10. CC Antya 18 (the water-pastimes seen by Mahaprabhu at the sea; the fisherman who "caught" Him in his net).
  11. A closing Sanskrit verse (probably of the scribe or editor); the date below it in the edition — Bengali year 1298, 30 Chaitra (= April 1892) — is the date of the edition, not of the composition.
